name: Shopproof: EU Withdrawal Button and GPSR for WooCommerce
author: shopproofapp

sections.description:
Shopproof helps WooCommerce shops that sell across EU borders keep track of consumer rules for Austria, Germany, France, Italy and the Netherlands, plus the rules that apply EU-wide.

Watch Shopproof in a demo shop in 72 seconds:

Shops outside the EU, for example in the US, the UK or Switzerland, that sell to EU consumers get the same features. Shopproof also shows them a checklist of the extra EU duties for sellers from abroad: the EU responsible person, import VAT and IOSS, the customs duty on small parcels, import charges before the order and the GDPR representative.

Shops that sell online to consumers in the EU need a withdrawal button (from 19 June 2026 in most countries, from 1 October 2026 in Austria): an easy way for customers to withdraw from a contract online (EU Directive 2023/2673). Shopproof adds it to WooCommerce for free, with the wording for each country: Widerrufsbutton (“Vertrag widerrufen”) in Germany and Austria, bouton de rétractation in France, pulsante di recesso in Italy and herroepingsknop in the Netherlands. It also adds the product safety details the General Product Safety Regulation (GPSR) asks for, and the EU legal guarantee notice.

Coming from Germanized, German Market or another withdrawal button plugin? The switch assistant moves you over in a safe order, with an undo for every step.

New in 0.35.0:

  • Fewer things to think about. The Overview offers ready-made answers to the questions the law asks of your shop, such as whether you take part in consumer dispute resolution, and suggests products to leave out of withdrawal. Nothing is ticked or saved until you press it.
  • One quiet email when something needs you, never the same list twice in a week. Setup steps stay on the Overview and are never mailed.
  • A weekly check that the withdrawal link is still on your shop’s pages. It only opens your own shop.
  • One button keeps the rules up to date: a daily check for new rules and automatic updates for Shopproof. The Overview says when the last check worked, and says so when it did not.
  • Since 0.34.0: set Shopproof up by talking to your AI assistant, and place every Shopproof piece as a block, an Elementor widget or a WPBakery element.

In your language:

  • Deutsch: kostenloser Widerrufsbutton für WooCommerce („Vertrag widerrufen“) mit Eingangsbestätigung, Muster-Widerrufsformular, Fristen zum Widerrufsrecht und Widerrufsliste, Kündigungsbutton (§ 312k BGB), Herstellerangaben und Produktsicherheit nach GPSR, Garantiehinweis und Haltbarkeitslabel, Grundpreis, Pfand und der niedrigste Preis der letzten 30 Tage (Omnibus). Für Shops in Deutschland und Österreich. Technische Hilfe, keine Rechtsberatung.
  • Français : bouton de rétractation gratuit pour WooCommerce, formulaire type de rétractation, bouton de résiliation en ligne, sécurité des produits (GPSR) et avis sur la garantie légale de conformité.
  • Italiano: pulsante di recesso gratuito per WooCommerce, modulo tipo di recesso, sicurezza dei prodotti (GPSR) e avviso sulla garanzia legale.
  • Nederlands: gratis herroepingsknop voor WooCommerce, modelformulier voor herroeping, productveiligheid (GPSR) en melding over de wettelijke garantie.

A withdrawal button alone is not enough. This is what the EU rules ask around it, and what the free plugin does for each:

  • Withdrawal button with a two-step confirmation (“Withdraw from contract here”, then “Confirm withdrawal”), in the legal wording for each country.
  • Acknowledgement on a durable medium: an email to the customer with the content, date and time of the withdrawal, plus a status page.
  • EU model withdrawal form (Directive 2011/83/EU, Annex I(B)), in every official EU language, filled in with your shop’s name, address and email.
  • 14 day deadline check from the delivery date, with the refund due date and a reminder.
  • Exclusions (Article 16) by product type and category, including sub-categories, with your own explanation.
  • Two separate consent boxes at checkout for downloads (Article 16(m)), saved on the order and repeated in the order email.
  • Tamper-evident proof: every withdrawal goes into a hash-chained proof log (SHA-256).
  • Partial withdrawals: customers tick the items they send back.
  • All 24 official EU languages for the withdrawal form and button.
  • CSV export of all withdrawals, and HPOS support.

Shopproof gives you the technical function. It does not make the legal call for your catalogue, and national rules can add to the EU baseline.

What this version does:

Setup and rules

  • A WooCommerce > Shopproof page in tabs. The Overview tab has a short setup checklist and one status card per feature that links to where you fix it. A small “Set up Shopproof” notice reminds you until setup is done, and you can hide it.
  • “Why is this needed?” fold-outs name the law, the date it applies from and link to the official text.
  • The Rules tab lists the rules Shopproof tracks for each region. The rules list ships with the plugin, so it works without contacting any server. You can download newer lists by hand or once a day; if a download fails, your current copy stays. Only rules that passed our review are shown.
  • An accessibility statement draft on the Accessibility tab, from your shop details, in English, German, French, Italian or Dutch.

Withdrawal button

  • A withdrawal page with an accessible form (one click creates it), and a “withdraw from contract” link in the site footer, the customer account, order details and order emails.
  • One-tap withdrawal: the link in order emails and on the order page is signed for that order, so name, email, order number and date are already filled in. The order number is optional; without one, the withdrawal is matched to the customer’s latest order.
  • Placement check: shows your own pages (home, product, shop, cart, account, withdrawal page) at desktop and phone width with the link outlined, and checks that it is visible, not covered, meets WCAG 2.2 AA contrast and appears only once. It runs in your browser; nothing leaves your site.
  • Each withdrawal is saved with date and time. The customer gets an acknowledgement email, you get a copy, and the order gets a note. If the email cannot be sent, the withdrawal says so with a button to send it again.
  • The withdrawal emails are WooCommerce emails you can edit under WooCommerce > Settings > Emails. Two optional emails tell the customer when the return arrived and when the refund was sent.
  • Options: a longer withdrawal period, a contact email, where the links show, required order number or date, an extra information field, and product types or categories you exclude (for example made-to-order goods) with your own explanation.
  • Link and button wording: the country’s legal wording by default, another reviewed wording, or your own text after a warning.
  • Partial withdrawals: customers tick the items they send back, with photos, once they enter their order number and email.
  • A status page for each customer shows when the withdrawal was received, the return arrived and the refund was sent. A WooCommerce refund of the whole order sets “Refund sent” by itself.
  • WooCommerce > Withdrawals lists every withdrawal, with CSV export and the WordPress personal data export and erase tools.
  • EU model withdrawal form with the [shopproof_model_form] shortcode, in all 23 official EU language versions, filled in with your shop’s name, address and email.
  • Deadline clock on every withdrawal: whether it arrived in time, the date the refund is due, and a reminder when a refund is due within three days or overdue. Part refunds show as “Partly refunded, check”.
  • Returns tools: add your Sendcloud, Returnless, 8returns, AfterShip or ReturnGO portal link to the acknowledgement email, and send each withdrawal to a signed webhook for your returns tool, Zapier, Make or n8n.
  • The button, form and consent boxes speak all 24 official EU languages (the newer languages were written with AI help and are not yet checked by native speakers).
  • Works alongside WooCommerce’s own withdrawal form (WooCommerce 11.1 and later) without adding a second form; its requests get Shopproof’s clocks, status page, emails and proof log.
  • Withdrawal policy check: reads your withdrawal policy page and compares the period and email address with your settings. When it cannot compare, it says “Not checked” with the reason.

Product pages

  • Product safety details (GPSR): enter the manufacturer and EU responsible person once for the shop, per brand (WooCommerce Brands, Perfect Brands, YITH Brands) or per product, also in bulk and by CSV import. They show as one line near Add to cart that opens to the full details, or in a “Product safety” tab. No “Powered by” credit.
  • Hazard labelling for chemicals sold online (CLP Article 48a): pictograms, signal word and the official hazard and precautionary statements in the shopper’s language.
  • The official EU legal guarantee notice (Regulation (EU) 2025/1960), unedited, with a text version for screen readers. Shortcode: [shopproof_guarantee_notice].
  • The EU durability label “GARAN” for products with a free producer durability guarantee of more than two years, set per product or once per brand, with a source link and a yearly check reminder. Shortcode: [shopproof_durability_label].
  • Registration numbers (WEEE, batteries, packaging, the French IDU, textiles) and how customers return old batteries and devices, on product pages, in the footer or with [shopproof_registrations]. Shopproof checks no registers.
  • Food information (EU Regulation 1169/2011) in a “Food information” tab: ingredients with allergens in bold, the 14 allergens, net quantity, storage, origin, Nutri-Score and the nutrition table rounded the EU way. Shortcode: [shopproof_food_information].
  • Unit prices (Grundpreis, Germany PAngV, Directive 98/6/EC): price per kg, l, m, m² or m³ below the price, also in lists and for variations. Off while Germanized or German Market show their own.
  • Bottle deposit (Pfand): set deposit types once, pick them per product or variation, and shoppers in that country see the deposit below the price and as its own cart line.
  • Price and delivery notes: “Incl. VAT, plus shipping”, small business or free shipping notices, delivery times, and margin scheme or known defects for used goods. Shortcode: [shopproof_price_notes].
  • Lowest price before a sale (EU Omnibus rules): Shopproof records your price changes and shows the lowest price of the 30 days before each sale. Off until you turn it on.
  • Energy labels and the French repairability or durability index, per product or variation, with the EPREL number and product information sheet. Shortcode: [shopproof_energy_label].
  • Review check notice (Unfair Commercial Practices Directive, Art. 7(6)): one line below the Reviews heading on how you check reviews. Shortcode: [shopproof_review_notice].
  • Green claims check (Directive (EU) 2024/825): lists products whose text uses generic environmental words such as “eco-friendly” or “klimaneutral”, in all 24 EU languages. Worth checking, never a verdict.

Cart, checkout and emails

  • Cart notes: a short description under each item and checkboxes shoppers tick before they order (withdrawal policy, privacy notice, up to three of your own). Which boxes were ticked, and when, is saved on the order.
  • Order button wording (Art. 8(2)), off by default: “Zahlungspflichtig bestellen” or “Order with obligation to pay” on the classic checkout and the Checkout block.
  • Delivery and payment line (Art. 8(3)), off by default: where you deliver and your payment methods, above Proceed to checkout.
  • Digital content consent (Article 16(m)): two separate ticks for downloads, saved on the order and repeated in the order emails (Article 8(7)). Classic checkout, and block checkout from WooCommerce 9.9.
  • Services, subscriptions and bookings: a “Right of withdrawal” type per product, service start boxes (Article 8(8)), and a suggested amount for a service already provided (Article 14(3) and (4)). Works with WooCommerce Subscriptions and WooCommerce Bookings, and without them.
  • Cancel button for subscriptions and memberships (Kündigungsbutton, Germany § 312k BGB, France online cancellation): footer and account links, a cancel page with the final “Cancel now” button, a confirmation email and WooCommerce > Cancellations. Off until you turn it on. Shortcode: [shopproof_cancel_form].
  • Legal pages in order emails: the order confirmation or completed order email can end with links to your terms, withdrawal policy and privacy notice.
  • Dispute resolution statement (Germany § 36 VSBG, France consumer mediator) with the [shopproof_dispute_statement] shortcode.

Records and switching

  • Proof log under WooCommerce > Proof log: a daily, dated record of what your withdrawal button, guarantee notice, product safety details and registration numbers showed, plus every withdrawal. Entries are hash-chained, so a later change shows up. Check the chain and download it as CSV. It stays in your own database.
  • Switch assistant under WooCommerce > Shopproof switch: moves you from Germanized, German Market or the EU Order Withdrawal Button in a safe order, with an undo for every step. Copies product safety details from Germanized without changing Germanized’s data, and maps common product safety columns in WooCommerce’s product importer.
  • Works with WooCommerce order storage (HPOS) and the block cart and checkout.
  • Deleting the plugin removes its settings. Withdrawal records, the proof log and product details are kept; add define( ‘SHOPPROOF_REMOVE_ALL_DATA’, true ); to wp-config.php before deleting to remove them too.

Shopproof gives technical help. It is not legal advice.

Everything in this plugin is free and stays free: no locked features, no trial periods and no limits on products. An optional paid add-on, Shopproof Pro, is sold separately at https://shopproof.app/pro/. It adds researched country rules, emails when a rule changes and outside proof of your log. This plugin works fully without it.

External services

Shopproof works without contacting any server. It contacts one only when you ask for it, in the two cases below. It ships with a copy of the Shopproof rules list, a JSON data file listing the EU and national consumer rules it shows (no code is downloaded or run). Because these rules change, you can choose to download newer copies of the list from the Shopproof rules service, run by Apex Point Consulting GmbH, the makers of this plugin. No account is needed.

  • When: only after you ask for it under WooCommerce > Shopproof > Rule updates, either by pressing “Check for rule updates now” or by turning on “Check for rule updates automatically once a day”. Nothing is downloaded when you install or activate the plugin, and automatic updates are off until you turn them on.
  • What is sent: a plain HTTPS request for the file. No shop data, customer data or personal data is sent. Like any web request, your server’s IP address is visible to the host.
  • Where: https://d3jn3nfc6dj1sm.cloudfront.net/rules/v1/rules.json, the Shopproof rules service, served through Amazon CloudFront.
  • Privacy policy: https://shopproof.app/privacy
  • Terms: https://shopproof.app/terms

If you send us a message with the form under “Help and contact” on the Overview tab, your shop sends what you typed to the Shopproof contact service, run by Apex Point Consulting GmbH.

  • When: only when you press “Send message”. Nothing is sent when the page opens.
  • What is sent: your name (optional), your email address and your message, your shop address if you leave that tick …
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce.
  2. Install and activate Shopproof.
  3. Open WooCommerce > Shopproof.
sections.faq:
How do I add the withdrawal button?

Open WooCommerce > Shopproof and press “Create the withdrawal page”. You can also place the form on any page with the Withdrawal form block or the [shopproof_withdrawal_form] shortcode, and a link with [shopproof_withdraw_link].

Where do I enter product safety details?

Shop-wide defaults are under WooCommerce > Shopproof > Product safety. Per product, open the product editor and use the “Product safety” panel. Per brand, open Products > Brands, edit the brand and fill in its Product safety fields: products of that brand without their own details use them before the shop-wide ones. A brand with a manufacturer but no responsible person means the maker is in the EU, so the shop-wide responsible person is not shown for it. The Product safety tab lists your brands and which have details. Under WooCommerce > Shopproof > Product safety you also choose where the block goes: one line near the Add to cart button (default) or a “Product safety” tab. You can also place the details anywhere with the [shopproof_product_safety] shortcode; add layout=”compact” for the one-line version.

For many products at once, select them in Products, choose Edit under Bulk actions and fill in the Product safety fields; empty fields change nothing. You can also use WooCommerce’s product CSV export and import: the file has a column for each product safety field.

Where do I enter my registration numbers?

Under WooCommerce > Shopproof > Registration numbers. Choose the kind of registration and its country, enter the number, and tick whether you sell batteries or electrical equipment to show the take-back information. Mark products on the General tab of the product editor with “Electrical equipment” or “Contains batteries”. The crossed-out wheeled bin symbol ships with the plugin.

Where does the legal guarantee notice come from?

The images in assets/guarantee are the official notices published in the Official Journal of the European Union (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1960, Annex I), unchanged. Reuse of EU documents is allowed under Commission Decision 2011/833/EU.

Where does the durability label come from?

The images in assets/durability are the official label and nested display from the Official Journal (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1960, Annex II), unchanged. Only the placeholder words are covered and replaced with your guarantee years, brand and model identifier, as the regulation allows. The text is set in Inter, the font the regulation asks for, Copyright 2016 The Inter Project Authors, licensed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (assets/durability/OFL.txt).

Where is the storefront script’s source?

The file assets/js/shopproof-widgets.js is shipped unminified. It is built from the Shopproof storefront widgets source and needs no build step to read or change.

Does it work with Germanized or German Market?

Yes. When Germanized, German Market or the EU Order Withdrawal Button adds its own withdrawal button, Shopproof adds no withdrawal links of its own, so customers never see two. Its product safety block stays hidden in the same way. You can choose to use Shopproof’s instead: the withdrawal button under WooCommerce > Shopproof > Withdrawal button, the product safety block under WooCommerce > Shopproof > Product safety. WooCommerce > Shopproof switch takes you through the move step by step and copies your product safety details from Germanized. Shopproof never changes those plugins’ settings or data, or your WooCommerce settings.

How do I connect my returns tool?

Open WooCommerce > Shopproof > Returns. Paste the link to your returns portal, and customers get it in their withdrawal acknowledgement. To create returns automatically, paste the address your returns tool gives you (or one from Zapier, Make or n8n) under “Send withdrawals automatically”, save, and press “Send a test withdrawal”. Each request is a JSON POST with the event name in the X-Shopproof-Event header and an X-Shopproof-Signature header (t= the Unix time, v1= the HMAC-SHA256 of the time, a dot and the request body, with your security key). If the address does not answer with a 2xx status, Shopproof tries again after 5 minutes, 1 hour and 6 hours, then emails you. Each withdrawal shows whether it was sent.

My shop is outside the EU. Does Shopproof help?

Yes. EU consumer rules apply when you sell to consumers in the EU, wherever your shop is. Shopproof works the same way for you. When your WooCommerce store address is outside the EU, the Overview tab also lists the extra duties for sellers from abroad, with the official sources. Shopproof cannot act as your EU responsible person, IOSS intermediary or GDPR representative; you appoint them yourself. Technical help, not legal or tax advice.

Can my AI assistant set up Shopproof for me?

Yes, if your assistant can use MCP servers from a config file (for example Claude Desktop or Cursor). Turn it on under WooCommerce > Shopproof > AI assistant and create a connection key. The assistant can then check your setup, switch on what your shop needs and answer questions such as “which refunds are overdue?”. It talks to your shop directly; this plugin sends nothing to us. It reads only until you turn on “Allow changes”, shows you every change before it is saved, and every change is recorded in the proof log and can be undone. Customer names and emails stay hidden unless you turn on “Include customer details”. What the assistant reads goes to the AI service you use, under that service’s terms. A connection key works only for this connection, not for the rest of your site, and stops working after 90 days, when a daily cleanup deletes it. Switching the connection off or deactivating the plugin deletes every key. Your site needs HTTPS for keys. On a multisite network, keys can be made only when Shopproof is network active.

What does Shopproof Pro add?

Shopproof Pro is a separate, paid add-on (https://shopproof.app/pro/). It emails you when a rule that affects your shop is added or changed, covers researched rules such as packaging and electrical goods registrations and the countries Spain, Poland and Belgium, keeps a calendar of the dates that matter, makes a proof pack PDF and stamps your proof log once a day outside your shop. Agencies get one dashboard for all their client shops. You do not need Pro: nothing in this plugin is locked, limited or time-limited. This plugin mentions Pro only on its own pages and its row on the Plugins screen, and the mentions go away when Pro is installed and active.

How do I get help or contact you?

On the Overview tab, under “Help and contact”, there are our step-by-step guides, the support forum here on WordPress.org and a short form that sends your message to support@shopproof.app. You can also write to support@shopproof.app from your own email.

Is this legal advice?

No. Shopproof gives technical help to show the information EU rules ask for. For legal questions, please ask a lawyer in your country.
sections.changelog:
0.36.0

  • New: returns and refunds in the proof log. Each time a withdrawal moves to Return arrived or Refund sent, the proof log records when, and whether you set it in Shopproof, a refund on the WooCommerce order did, or the order’s “Order actions” shortcut. A refund day you enter for a refund outside WooCommerce is recorded too. For refunds the entry also holds the day the refund was due, whether it was paid by then, and the amount refunded against what the withdrawn items cost. No names, email addresses or order numbers, as for the withdrawals already in the log. Technical help, not legal advice.
  • New: delivery cost check. When the customer withdraws from every item and the refunds on the order give back every item but not the delivery cost, Shopproof no longer marks the withdrawal as Refund sent by itself. The withdrawal box says how much delivery cost is still open: the standard delivery cost is refunded too when every item comes back (Directive 2011/83/EU, Article 13(1)); only the extra cost of a dearer delivery the customer chose may be kept. Refund the rest on the order, or set Refund sent yourself when the refund is complete.
  • New: amount check. When refunds by item close a withdrawal but give back less than the withdrawn items cost, the withdrawal box names both amounts. A deduction for a loss in value can be right, so this is a note to check, never a block. The box also says that the customer pays the cost of sending goods back only if you told them so before the order.
  • Changed: the unit price check on the Product pages tab now looks at every published product, not only the first 100, and at each variation’s own size or weight (such as “5 l”). It reads the names straight from the database and only opens products whose names give a weight or volume, so the page stays quick; on a very large shop it pauses after 10 seconds, says how many of how many products it has checked so far and goes on from there the next time you open the page. If the products cannot be read from the database, it says Not checked with the reason, never that all is fine.
  • Fix: the check missed variations whose size is part of the variation’s own name in WooCommerce (such as “Olive oil – 5 l”).
  • New: add-ons can offer their own settings to the AI assistant, with the same preview, change list, proof log and undo. Shopproof Pro 0.18.0 uses this for the three product duty questions.
  • Technical help, not legal advice.

0.35.1

  • Fix: on PHP 8.6 with debug logging on, Shopproof no longer writes a “deprecated” notice to the log on every page. Nothing changes for your shop or your customers.
  • Tested with WordPress 7.2.

0.35.0

  • New: ready-made answers on the Overview tab. The dispute statement (“we do not take part”, as most small shops answer) and the review check notice (the answer that matches your WooCommerce review settings) are written out with the words your customers will see. Tick each one that is true for your shop and save; nothing is ticked or saved for you. Shops in France are not offered “we do not take part”, and the review answer only shows while product reviews are on.
  • New: suggested withdrawal exclusions on the Overview tab. Shopproof looks for goods the law lets you exclude from withdrawal: downloadable products while your download consent boxes are on, and product categories whose names suggest made to order or personalised goods, or sealed hygiene goods (in the seven admin languages). Each suggestion has its reason and an unticked box; only what you tick is excluded, and you can hide the suggestions for good. Whether an exception applies is your call. Technical help, not legal advice.
  • New: one quiet email when something needs you. Once a day Shopproof looks at the Overview, and only when a card says “Needs action” (a refund due today or late, a customer confirmation that could not be sent, no working withdrawal page, a link check that found a problem) or a refund is due in the next 3 days, it sends one email with a link to each fix to the address that gets the withdrawal copies. It goes through your shop’s own mailer, at most once a day, and the same list is not sent again within 7 days. Setup steps (such as a withdrawal page not chosen yet on a fresh install), “Needs a look” cards and anything Shopproof could not check never send an email. On by default, with an off switch under the answer on the Overview; nothing is scheduled until you open the WordPress admin.
  • New: weekly link check. Once a week your own site opens your home page and newest product page as a visitor would and looks for the withdrawal link (Shopproof’s link, or any link to your withdrawal page, also behind a language part such as /de). A page that only has a link with withdrawal words, such as a footer link to your withdrawal policy, counts as not checked. Redirects are followed only on your own site, including the step from http to https. If a theme or menu change removed it, the withdrawal card on the Overview says “Needs action” and the quiet email tells you. Only your own pages are opened, from your own server; nothing goes to another server. A page that does not open, or a shop in “Coming soon” mode, counts as not checked, never as missing. It starts once your withdrawal page works. The full check on the Withdrawal button tab is unchanged.
  • New: rules that arrive by themselves. While new rules reach your shop only with plugin updates, the Rules card on the Overview asks for one press of “Keep rules up to date”. That turns on the daily rule check (it sends no shop, customer or order data) and WordPress’s own automatic updates for Shopproof. Afterwards the card says “New rules arrive by themselves. Nothing for you to do.” with the date of the last check. If a check did not work, or none worked in the last 2 days, the card says so instead of showing the rules as fine. Nothing is switched on without that press; each part can be turned off on the Rules tab or the Plugins screen.
  • New: brands from your catalogue. Brands kept as a product attribute (such as Brand, Marke or Hersteller) now get product safety details once per brand, like WooCommerce Brands. The Product safety card on the Overview names the brands that still have no details, so you fill in each brand once instead of each product.
  • Technical help, not legal advice.

0.34.1

  • Fixed: the AI assistant could not save or undo a change on sites whose database is SQLite (such as WordPress Playground and the WordPress.org Live Preview). Every change answered “Another change is being saved”. It now works there too, still one change at a time. Shops on MySQL or MariaDB were not affected.
  • Fixed: the “Changes made by assistants” list on the AI assistant tab now shows each change in your admin language, with the names you see on the settings screens (for example “Legal guarantee notice”) instead of internal names such as “guarantee”.

0.34.0

  • New: blocks for the block editor and the site editor. Every Shopproof piece that had a shortcode is now also a block with a live preview, in its own Shopproof group: withdrawal form and link, model withdrawal form, cancel form, dispute statement, legal guarantee notice, registration numbers, review check notice, and for product templates product safety, durability label, energy label, food information and price notes. Search for them in your own words, also in German, French, Italian or Dutch (“Widerruf”, “Impressum”, “GPSR”). When you place a product block in your product template, Shopproof stops adding that piece by itself, so it shows once, where you put it. New withdrawal and cancel pages use the block. Your shortcodes keep working.
  • New: Elementor widgets. The same 13 pieces are in a Shopproof group of Elementor’s widget panel, found by the same search words. On product pages built with Elementor Pro’s product templates, the durability label, the product safety line and the price notes now follow Elementor’s own Add to cart and Price widgets, unless you place the Shopproof widget yourself.
  • New: Norwegian hazard labels. On pages in Norwegian (bokmål, nynorsk), the hazard label shows Norway’s official Norwegian texts for the statements, signal word and pictogram names, from the EEA texts of the CLP Regulation. Twelve combined statements, such as H302+H312+H332, have no official Norwegian text yet; a label that needs one shows in English as a whole, never in two languages. Rules data 0.19.0. Technical help, not legal advice.
  • New: WPBakery elements. The same 13 pieces are in a Shopproof tab of WPBakery’s Add element window, with the same options as the blocks.
  • Improved: product pages drawn by a page builder’s own product template, such as those of Divi, Bricks and Beaver Themer. These templates skip the WooCommerce spot where Shopproof placed the price notes, the durability label and the product safety line, so these could be missing. When the builder’s price and Add to cart parts use WooCommerce’s own price and Add to cart (as those builders’ WooCommerce parts do), the pieces now follow them, in the same order as on a WooCommerce product page, once each, and not where you placed them yourself (as a shortcode, block or widget). Tested on a WooCommerce shop with a template drawn that way and with the free Beaver Builder; Divi and Bricks themselves are paid and were not tested. The legal guarantee notice and registration numbers are not added to such templates, and the durability label and safety line need an Add to cart part: otherwise place the Shopproof shortcodes yourself.
  • New: works alongside legal text plugins from Händlerbund, IT-Recht Kanzlei, janolaw, avalex and getLaw. When one of them fills or prints your withdrawal policy page, the withdrawal options form says so, keeps comparing the published text, and tells you to fix a difference in Shopproof or with the provider, not on the page (Händlerbund’s update replaces page edits). With no policy page chosen yet, it lists the pages the plugin fills. Nothing is sent anywhere. Technical help, not legal advice.
  • New: set up Shopproof with your AI assistant. Under WooCommerce > Shopproof > AI assistant you can let an assistant that supports MCP (Claude Desktop, Cursor and others) check your setup, switch on what your shop needs, create the withdrawal page and answer questions about withdrawals and the proof log. Off until you turn it on, read only until you allow changes, a preview before every change, every change in the proof log with an undo, and customer names and emails only when you allow them. The assistant connects to your shop directly; nothing is sent to us.
  • New: moving from Omnibus by iWorks? The switch assistant (WooCommerce > Shopproof switch) copies its price history into Shopproof’s, so the lowest price of the 30 days before a sale is known from the first day. Only changes from before Shopproof’s own history are added, and they get their own seal in the proof log that names Omnibus. Then one button shows the Shopproof lowest price line instead, with an undo.
  • New: moving from GPSR for WooCommerce by WP Desk? The switch assistant copies each product’s manufacturer (or trade mark) and text instructions into Shopproof’s fields, and the importer as EU responsible person if you tick it. Products with their own Shopproof details keep them. While GPSR for WooCommerce is active, Shopproof leaves product safety details to it until you choose Shopproof’s.
  • The other plugins’ data is only read, never changed.
  • Swiss German: the admin screens now quote with « », as Swiss German writes it. German: “…” replaces three dots in loading texts, numbers and units keep together, and Pro is called an “Add-on”, as the German WordPress style guide and glossary ask.
  • Technical help, not legal advice.

0.33.0

  • New: the Overview tab opens with one answer: “Nothing for you to do right now”, or how many things need you, each by name with a link to where you fix it, most urgent first. A refund that is due today, late or due in the next 3 days comes first, and withdrawals that still wait for a refund are counted. Anything Shopproof could not check is listed as “Not checked”, never as fine, and the answer never reads “nothing to do” while setup is open. Refunds have a card of their own, so a withdrawal receipt that could not be sent no longer hides a refund deadline.
  • New: “Switch on what your shop needs” on the Overview tab. Shopproof reads your shop’s facts (shop country, goods and downloads, tax settings, shipping and payment methods, other plugins that already do the job) and lists only the features they call for that are still off: the legal guarantee notice, the VAT and shipping notes for shops in Germany and Austria, the lowest price before a sale, the delivery and payment line, the order button wording and the two download consent boxes. Each line says where it shows. One press switches them on; one Undo puts your settings back for 14 days. Nothing changes until you press the button. Choices only you can make, such as a longer withdrawal period, exclusions or your dispute statement, are never switched on for you.
  • New: Sell on eBay or Amazon, on the Product safety tab. Shopproof puts your product safety details (manufacturer and EU responsible person, GPSR) into the marketplaces’ own upload files, so you do not type them in again. For eBay, download the “Edit price and quantity” file in Seller Hub Reports, choose it here and upload the file you get back: Shopproof adds eBay’s manufacturer and responsible person columns, matched by SKU (eBay: Custom label). For Amazon, Shopproof makes a contacts file to enter once in Seller Central and a listings file with the contact email columns for the inventory file. Listings Shopproof cannot fill completely are left out and listed with the reason, because eBay removes details that are sent blank. Nothing is sent to eBay, Amazon or us.
  • New: Spanish and Polish for the texts your customers see: the hazard label (official texts of the CLP Regulation, Annex III to V), the EU legal guarantee notice (the official image and text version from Regulation (EU) 2025/1960), the durability label, the take-back information and the shop notes show in Spanish or Polish on sites in these languages. Before, they showed English.
  • Changed: the withdrawal line in Spanish and Polish order emails now ends with the short reminder, as in the other five languages.
  • New: the same customer texts in Swedish, Danish, Finnish, Portuguese, Hungarian and Greek on sites in these languages, and the withdrawal reminder in order emails in these languages too. Where the official EU texts had clear typing errors, the plugin shows the corrected words; the rules data lists each correction. The admin screens stay in seven languages.
  • New: an optional “Withdrawal form by Shopproof” line in small print at the very bottom of the customer’s withdrawal confirmation email and status page, in the customer’s language (all 24 official EU languages). Off unless you tick it under Withdrawal options. The word Shopproof links to shopproof.app with no tracking, and nothing is sent to Shopproof.
  • Rules data 0.18.0. The new texts were written with AI help and are not yet checked by native speakers.
  • Technical help, not legal advice.

They follow the language you chose in your WordPress profile (Users > Profile > Language), or the site language. Formal address throughout (Sie, vous, Lei, u, usted). German has its own build for Switzerland (with “ss”) and for formal German WordPress. The translations ship inside the plugin, so they work without a WordPress.org language pack; if one appears later, it comes first and the plugin’s own texts fill the gaps.
  • Changed: on shops whose site language is one of the six, the few shop and email texts that were still English now use these translations. Texts in the customer’s own language stay as before.
  • New: once setup has been complete for 7 days, the Overview tab asks once for a review on WordPress.org. “Not now” hides it for 90 days and “Do not ask again” hides it for good. Every feature stays free either way.

Turn on the line on the Product pages tab, and every reduced price shows the lowest price of the 30 days before the sale, or the lowest since a newer product was added. Nothing shows while Shopproof has less than 30 days of a product’s prices; for sales that began earlier you can type the lowest price on the product. The history starts with this update.

When Germanized or German Market is active, they keep the button. The Overview says what your button says now.
  • New: delivery and payment line (Art. 8(3)), off by default. One line in the shopper’s language with where you deliver (or how many countries, over 12), your own words on restrictions and your active payment methods, above Proceed to checkout, at the top of the classic checkout and after the Cart and Checkout blocks.

Worth checking, never a verdict. Nothing is stored.
  • New: accessibility statement draft on the Accessibility tab, from your shop details in English, German, French, Italian or Dutch, with the authority for Austria, Germany, France, Italy and the Netherlands. Copy it, or save it as a draft page. The placement check notes on each page whether it links to accessibility information.
  • New: shops outside the EU and EEA (store address outside) get an Overview section with the extra EU duties for sellers from abroad and their official sources: EU responsible person (checked against the Product safety tab), import VAT and IOSS, the EUR 3 customs duty per item, the EUR 2 Union handling fee per item, import charges before the order and the GDPR representative.
  • New: the withdrawal policy check also says whether your withdrawal policy page tells customers they can withdraw online, and shows the official sentence in your language to copy when it is missing.

  • New: the deadline clock reads the carrier’s delivery day from Germanized or Shiptastic shipments and TrackShip with Advanced Shipment Tracking. A day you enter yourself still wins.
  • Changed: a refund no longer shows as overdue while the goods are not back (Art. 13(3)). After the 14 days it says “Refund waits for the goods” until you set Return arrived or the customer shows proof of sending. Orders of only services keep the 14 days.
  • Changed: withdrawals from an order with a company name or VAT number show a “Business order?” note. Shopproof never refuses a withdrawal for this.
  • Changed: the daily proof log record now holds every shop and shopper facing setting and the result of your last placement check. Free text you typed is not repeated, only whether it is set.
  • Rules list 0.16.0: green claims (0.13.0), duties for sellers outside the EU (0.14.0 and 0.16.0) and the official online withdrawal sentence in all 24 EU languages (0.15.0).
  • Technical help, not legal advice.

0.30.0

  • New: “Help and contact” at the end of the Overview tab, with our guides, the support forum and a short form to send us a message. Your name and email address are filled in from your profile and you can change them. Nothing is sent until you press “Send message”. With Shopproof Pro you get an answer within 1 working day. The Help panel at the top right and the Plugins screen link to it.
  • Fixed: the email to your shop after the last failed try to reach your returns tool now says the customer has their acknowledgement only when it was sent, asks you to send one when it failed, and claims nothing when Shopproof does not know.

Works with WooCommerce Subscriptions and WooCommerce Bookings, and without them.

short_description: Free EU withdrawal button (Widerrufsbutton), GPSR product safety, guarantee notice and proof log for WooCommerce. Set up with your AI assistant.
description:
Shopproof helps WooCommerce shops that sell across EU borders keep track of consumer rules for Austria, Germany, France, Italy and the Netherlands, plus the rules that apply EU-wide.

Watch Shopproof in a demo shop in 72 seconds:

Shops outside the EU, for example in the US, the UK or Switzerland, that sell to EU consumers get the same features. Shopproof also shows them a checklist of the extra EU duties for sellers from abroad: the EU responsible person, import VAT and IOSS, the customs duty on small parcels, import charges before the order and the GDPR representative.

Shops that sell online to consumers in the EU need a withdrawal button (from 19 June 2026 in most countries, from 1 October 2026 in Austria): an easy way for customers to withdraw from a contract online (EU Directive 2023/2673). Shopproof adds it to WooCommerce for free, with the wording for each country: Widerrufsbutton (“Vertrag widerrufen”) in Germany and Austria, bouton de rétractation in France, pulsante di recesso in Italy and herroepingsknop in the Netherlands. It also adds the product safety details the General Product Safety Regulation (GPSR) asks for, and the EU legal guarantee notice.

Coming from Germanized, German Market or another withdrawal button plugin? The switch assistant moves you over in a safe order, with an undo for every step.

New in 0.35.0:

  • Fewer things to think about. The Overview offers ready-made answers to the questions the law asks of your shop, such as whether you take part in consumer dispute resolution, and suggests products to leave out of withdrawal. Nothing is ticked or saved until you press it.
  • One quiet email when something needs you, never the same list twice in a week. Setup steps stay on the Overview and are never mailed.
  • A weekly check that the withdrawal link is still on your shop’s pages. It only opens your own shop.
  • One button keeps the rules up to date: a daily check for new rules and automatic updates for Shopproof. The Overview says when the last check worked, and says so when it did not.
  • Since 0.34.0: set Shopproof up by talking to your AI assistant, and place every Shopproof piece as a block, an Elementor widget or a WPBakery element.

In your language:

  • Deutsch: kostenloser Widerrufsbutton für WooCommerce („Vertrag widerrufen“) mit Eingangsbestätigung, Muster-Widerrufsformular, Fristen zum Widerrufsrecht und Widerrufsliste, Kündigungsbutton (§ 312k BGB), Herstellerangaben und Produktsicherheit nach GPSR, Garantiehinweis und Haltbarkeitslabel, Grundpreis, Pfand und der niedrigste Preis der letzten 30 Tage (Omnibus). Für Shops in Deutschland und Österreich. Technische Hilfe, keine Rechtsberatung.
  • Français : bouton de rétractation gratuit pour WooCommerce, formulaire type de rétractation, bouton de résiliation en ligne, sécurité des produits (GPSR) et avis sur la garantie légale de conformité.
  • Italiano: pulsante di recesso gratuito per WooCommerce, modulo tipo di recesso, sicurezza dei prodotti (GPSR) e avviso sulla garanzia legale.
  • Nederlands: gratis herroepingsknop voor WooCommerce, modelformulier voor herroeping, productveiligheid (GPSR) en melding over de wettelijke garantie.

A withdrawal button alone is not enough. This is what the EU rules ask around it, and what the free plugin does for each:

  • Withdrawal button with a two-step confirmation (“Withdraw from contract here”, then “Confirm withdrawal”), in the legal wording for each country.
  • Acknowledgement on a durable medium: an email to the customer with the content, date and time of the withdrawal, plus a status page.
  • EU model withdrawal form (Directive 2011/83/EU, Annex I(B)), in every official EU language, filled in with your shop’s name, address and email.
  • 14 day deadline check from the delivery date, with the refund due date and a reminder.
  • Exclusions (Article 16) by product type and category, including sub-categories, with your own explanation.
  • Two separate consent boxes at checkout for downloads (Article 16(m)), saved on the order and repeated in the order email.
  • Tamper-evident proof: every withdrawal goes into a hash-chained proof log (SHA-256).
  • Partial withdrawals: customers tick the items they send back.
  • All 24 official EU languages for the withdrawal form and button.
  • CSV export of all withdrawals, and HPOS support.

Shopproof gives you the technical function. It does not make the legal call for your catalogue, and national rules can add to the EU baseline.

What this version does:

Setup and rules

  • A WooCommerce > Shopproof page in tabs. The Overview tab has a short setup checklist and one status card per feature that links to where you fix it. A small “Set up Shopproof” notice reminds you until setup is done, and you can hide it.
  • “Why is this needed?” fold-outs name the law, the date it applies from and link to the official text.
  • The Rules tab lists the rules Shopproof tracks for each region. The rules list ships with the plugin, so it works without contacting any server. You can download newer lists by hand or once a day; if a download fails, your current copy stays. Only rules that passed our review are shown.
  • An accessibility statement draft on the Accessibility tab, from your shop details, in English, German, French, Italian or Dutch.

Withdrawal button

  • A withdrawal page with an accessible form (one click creates it), and a “withdraw from contract” link in the site footer, the customer account, order details and order emails.
  • One-tap withdrawal: the link in order emails and on the order page is signed for that order, so name, email, order number and date are already filled in. The order number is optional; without one, the withdrawal is matched to the customer’s latest order.
  • Placement check: shows your own pages (home, product, shop, cart, account, withdrawal page) at desktop and phone width with the link outlined, and checks that it is visible, not covered, meets WCAG 2.2 AA contrast and appears only once. It runs in your browser; nothing leaves your site.
  • Each withdrawal is saved with date and time. The customer gets an acknowledgement email, you get a copy, and the order gets a note. If the email cannot be sent, the withdrawal says so with a button to send it again.
  • The withdrawal emails are WooCommerce emails you can edit under WooCommerce > Settings > Emails. Two optional emails tell the customer when the return arrived and when the refund was sent.
  • Options: a longer withdrawal period, a contact email, where the links show, required order number or date, an extra information field, and product types or categories you exclude (for example made-to-order goods) with your own explanation.
  • Link and button wording: the country’s legal wording by default, another reviewed wording, or your own text after a warning.
  • Partial withdrawals: customers tick the items they send back, with photos, once they enter their order number and email.
  • A status page for each customer shows when the withdrawal was received, the return arrived and the refund was sent. A WooCommerce refund of the whole order sets “Refund sent” by itself.
  • WooCommerce > Withdrawals lists every withdrawal, with CSV export and the WordPress personal data export and erase tools.
  • EU model withdrawal form with the [shopproof_model_form] shortcode, in all 23 official EU language versions, filled in with your shop’s name, address and email.
  • Deadline clock on every withdrawal: whether it arrived in time, the date the refund is due, and a reminder when a refund is due within three days or overdue. Part refunds show as “Partly refunded, check”.
  • Returns tools: add your Sendcloud, Returnless, 8returns, AfterShip or ReturnGO portal link to the acknowledgement email, and send each withdrawal to a signed webhook for your returns tool, Zapier, Make or n8n.
  • The button, form and consent boxes speak all 24 official EU languages (the newer languages were written with AI help and are not yet checked by native speakers).
  • Works alongside WooCommerce’s own withdrawal form (WooCommerce 11.1 and later) without adding a second form; its requests get Shopproof’s clocks, status page, emails and proof log.
  • Withdrawal policy check: reads your withdrawal policy page and compares the period and email address with your settings. When it cannot compare, it says “Not checked” with the reason.

Product pages

  • Product safety details (GPSR): enter the manufacturer and EU responsible person once for the shop, per brand (WooCommerce Brands, Perfect Brands, YITH Brands) or per product, also in bulk and by CSV import. They show as one line near Add to cart that opens to the full details, or in a “Product safety” tab. No “Powered by” credit.
  • Hazard labelling for chemicals sold online (CLP Article 48a): pictograms, signal word and the official hazard and precautionary statements in the shopper’s language.
  • The official EU legal guarantee notice (Regulation (EU) 2025/1960), unedited, with a text version for screen readers. Shortcode: [shopproof_guarantee_notice].
  • The EU durability label “GARAN” for products with a free producer durability guarantee of more than two years, set per product or once per brand, with a source link and a yearly check reminder. Shortcode: [shopproof_durability_label].
  • Registration numbers (WEEE, batteries, packaging, the French IDU, textiles) and how customers return old batteries and devices, on product pages, in the footer or with [shopproof_registrations]. Shopproof checks no registers.
  • Food information (EU Regulation 1169/2011) in a “Food information” tab: ingredients with allergens in bold, the 14 allergens, net quantity, storage, origin, Nutri-Score and the nutrition table rounded the EU way. Shortcode: [shopproof_food_information].
  • Unit prices (Grundpreis, Germany PAngV, Directive 98/6/EC): price per kg, l, m, m² or m³ below the price, also in lists and for variations. Off while Germanized or German Market show their own.
  • Bottle deposit (Pfand): set deposit types once, pick them per product or variation, and shoppers in that country see the deposit below the price and as its own cart line.
  • Price and delivery notes: “Incl. VAT, plus shipping”, small business or free shipping notices, delivery times, and margin scheme or known defects for used goods. Shortcode: [shopproof_price_notes].
  • Lowest price before a sale (EU Omnibus rules): Shopproof records your price changes and shows the lowest price of the 30 days before each sale. Off until you turn it on.
  • Energy labels and the French repairability or durability index, per product or variation, with the EPREL number and product information sheet. Shortcode: [shopproof_energy_label].
  • Review check notice (Unfair Commercial Practices Directive, Art. 7(6)): one line below the Reviews heading on how you check reviews. Shortcode: [shopproof_review_notice].
  • Green claims check (Directive (EU) 2024/825): lists products whose text uses generic environmental words such as “eco-friendly” or “klimaneutral”, in all 24 EU languages. Worth checking, never a verdict.

Cart, checkout and emails

  • Cart notes: a short description under each item and checkboxes shoppers tick before they order (withdrawal policy, privacy notice, up to three of your own). Which boxes were ticked, and when, is saved on the order.
  • Order button wording (Art. 8(2)), off by default: “Zahlungspflichtig bestellen” or “Order with obligation to pay” on the classic checkout and the Checkout block.
  • Delivery and payment line (Art. 8(3)), off by default: where you deliver and your payment methods, above Proceed to checkout.
  • Digital content consent (Article 16(m)): two separate ticks for downloads, saved on the order and repeated in the order emails (Article 8(7)). Classic checkout, and block checkout from WooCommerce 9.9.
  • Services, subscriptions and bookings: a “Right of withdrawal” type per product, service start boxes (Article 8(8)), and a suggested amount for a service already provided (Article 14(3) and (4)). Works with WooCommerce Subscriptions and WooCommerce Bookings, and without them.
  • Cancel button for subscriptions and memberships (Kündigungsbutton, Germany § 312k BGB, France online cancellation): footer and account links, a cancel page with the final “Cancel now” button, a confirmation email and WooCommerce > Cancellations. Off until you turn it on. Shortcode: [shopproof_cancel_form].
  • Legal pages in order emails: the order confirmation or completed order email can end with links to your terms, withdrawal policy and privacy notice.
  • Dispute resolution statement (Germany § 36 VSBG, France consumer mediator) with the [shopproof_dispute_statement] shortcode.

Records and switching

  • Proof log under WooCommerce > Proof log: a daily, dated record of what your withdrawal button, guarantee notice, product safety details and registration numbers showed, plus every withdrawal. Entries are hash-chained, so a later change shows up. Check the chain and download it as CSV. It stays in your own database.
  • Switch assistant under WooCommerce > Shopproof switch: moves you from Germanized, German Market or the EU Order Withdrawal Button in a safe order, with an undo for every step. Copies product safety details from Germanized without changing Germanized’s data, and maps common product safety columns in WooCommerce’s product importer.
  • Works with WooCommerce order storage (HPOS) and the block cart and checkout.
  • Deleting the plugin removes its settings. Withdrawal records, the proof log and product details are kept; add define( ‘SHOPPROOF_REMOVE_ALL_DATA’, true ); to wp-config.php before deleting to remove them too.

Shopproof gives technical help. It is not legal advice.

Everything in this plugin is free and stays free: no locked features, no trial periods and no limits on products. An optional paid add-on, Shopproof Pro, is sold separately at https://shopproof.app/pro/. It adds researched country rules, emails when a rule changes and outside proof of your log. This plugin works fully without it.

External services

Shopproof works without contacting any server. It contacts one only when you ask for it, in the two cases below. It ships with a copy of the Shopproof rules list, a JSON data file listing the EU and national consumer rules it shows (no code is downloaded or run). Because these rules change, you can choose to download newer copies of the list from the Shopproof rules service, run by Apex Point Consulting GmbH, the makers of this plugin. No account is needed.

  • When: only after you ask for it under WooCommerce > Shopproof > Rule updates, either by pressing “Check for rule updates now” or by turning on “Check for rule updates automatically once a day”. Nothing is downloaded when you install or activate the plugin, and automatic updates are off until you turn them on.
  • What is sent: a plain HTTPS request for the file. No shop data, customer data or personal data is sent. Like any web request, your server’s IP address is visible to the host.
  • Where: https://d3jn3nfc6dj1sm.cloudfront.net/rules/v1/rules.json, the Shopproof rules service, served through Amazon CloudFront.
  • Privacy policy: https://shopproof.app/privacy
  • Terms: https://shopproof.app/terms

If you send us a message with the form under “Help and contact” on the Overview tab, your shop sends what you typed to the Shopproof contact service, run by Apex Point Consulting GmbH.

  • When: only when you press “Send message”. Nothing is sent when the page opens.
  • What is sent: your name (optional), your email address and your message, your shop address if you leave that tick …
